sections.heading: Glamsterdam Devnet 8: Platåberget Attack Impact
sections.summary: Jochem's JUMPDEST contract spam knocked out 12/13 Besu nodes; all clients except Geth and Nethermind should investigate performance.
sections.body:
- The Platåberget test case deployed ~100k contracts (64 KB each, filled with JUMPDEST) over a week, then spammed full-block zero-calldata transactions that loop-call ~66,667 of those contracts repeatedly.
  - Contracts have unique code hashes; each requires 64 KB of JUMPDEST analysis.
  - The attack cycles over the same accounts, so cached state should be warm — making the failures more concerning since it is not an IO/state problem.
- Besu was hit hardest: 12/13 nodes went offline; ~65% of proposals missed over the weekend. Nimbus-EL was second worst. Nethermind missed 5% and Geth only 0.1%.
- Besu team (Ameziane) is investigating: initial analysis points to a memory spike, possibly related to debug trace code paths that are not yet optimized. A PR to fix the unoptimized trace code path exists but is not merged.
  - Stefan has disabled traces/debug on some Besu nodes to allow comparison; spam scenario is running again.
- Hardware: 8 cores, 16 GB RAM on DigitalOcean. CPerezz noted this is below [EIP-7870](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7870) recommended specs. Tracoor was requesting traces from every node, adding load.
- Toni also published worst-case payloads and BALs (maximum blob KZG openings, maximum BAL size) into different slots; this surfaced a Nimbus PTC voting-too-early issue, still under investigation.
- Jochem shared a corresponding benchmarker test case in the all-EL Discord channel and will ping Besu and other clients.
  - Test name: `benchmark/stateful/bloatnet/test_account_query.py::test_account_access[fork_Amsterdam-...-gas-value_200M]`
- Spencer asked about a shared repository for devnet attack configs. PK noted spamoor configs are already in the repo frontend; Jochem will add his attacks there. Toni noted spamoor is not flexible enough for cross-layer CL-level attacks.
  - Follow-up: Marius pointed out attack payloads can be multiple GBs, making storage challenging.

sections.heading: Glamsterdam Devnet 9: Unplanned Non-Finality
sections.summary: Devnet 9 (1,000 nodes) never reached planned non-finality trigger; Prysm trunk branches lacked alpha.14 changes, causing ~30% of nodes to fail at fork transition.
sections.body:
- Devnet 9 was a 1,000-node network with ~4 million validator keys, intended for non-finality testing. The network experienced ~28 hours of unplanned non-finality before recovery on Sep 3.
- Root cause: Prysm trunk branches did not include the latest alpha.14 spec changes, so ~30% of the network went offline at the Gloas fork transition.
  - Prysm fix PR: [OffchainLabs/prysm#17382](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17382) — not yet merged to trunk; still has review feedback.
  - Additional Prysm PR needed for builder deposits: [OffchainLabs/prysm#17440](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17440).
- Lighthouse OOM issue: restarting Lighthouse nodes during non-finality caused hash caching inefficiency, leading to OOM crashes even with 32 GB RAM. Root cause analysis shared by EthPandaOps.
- Builder nodes also struggled due to subscription to all sub-networks.
- L2s did not get adequate time to test fork transition because the network was not finalizing.
- Network was shut down early due to cost and incomplete client readiness; most post-mortem discussions are happening async.

sections.heading: Glamsterdam Devnet 11 Launch Readiness
sections.summary: Devnet 11 targets midweek launch as a happy-path fork-transition network for L2s; blocked on Prysm merging alpha.14 to trunk.
sections.body:
- Devnet 11 is planned as a happy-path network: no stress testing during fork transition, so L2s and tooling teams can test cleanly.
- All clients must be on trunk/unstable branches. Currently blocked on Prysm merging the alpha.14 update.
- EL test readiness: EIP-7610 removed in [tests-glamsterdam-devnet@v8.1.3](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/releases#release-tests-glamsterdam-devnet@v8.1.3) and [tests@v20.0.2](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/releases#release-tests@v20.0.2). EIP-8037 merge-time state-gas repayment rule updated in [tests-glamsterdam-devnet@v8.1.4](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/releases#release-tests-glamsterdam-devnet@v8.1.4).
- Timeline: midweek to end of week launch, then 1–2 days (≥24 hours) from genesis to Gloas fork activation to give L2s preparation time.
- Validator set size and exact configuration to be decided by PK and Rafael. Will not use the large 4M-validator set from devnet 9.
- Watchtower updates will be managed more carefully to avoid destabilizing the network as happened on devnet 9.
- Nico offered deposit attack scripts but PK asked to keep devnet 11 as happy path since L2s want to test.

sections.heading: EIP-8253: Bump Nonce of Zero-Nonce Storage Accounts
sections.summary: Decision deferred to Thursday ACD call; most clients lean toward Hegota inclusion, viewing Glamsterdam as too late.
sections.body:
- Jochem presented [EIP-8253](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8253): 28 mainnet accounts have nonce 0, no code, but non-empty storage. The BAL spec assumes creating a contract on such an account starts with an empty tree, but applying a BAL state diff without re-execution would incorrectly delete existing storage keys (pre-images unknown).
  - TL;DR gist: <https://gist.github.com/jochem-brouwer/72b97452ba440da909e5da5bdf876817>
  - Draft EELS spec+tests PR: [execution-specs#3535](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3535)
- Toni argued that the BAL contains post-state diffs and doesn't care about prior storage, so nothing actually breaks today. However, including EIP-8253 would also require adding nonce changes to the BAL at the fork boundary, creating new BAL interaction.
- Client team positions:
  - Nethermind (FLCL): too late for Glamsterdam; not enough fork transitions to test properly. Hegota at least.
  - Geth (Marius): not deeply familiar; concerned about BAL tech debt if deferred, but fine with Hegota if no debt is introduced.
  - Besu (Ben Adams): pre-fork block idea floated but acknowledged as too late; accounts are small (~40 storage slots max), so BAL impact is minimal. Fine waiting.
  - RETH (Dragan Rakita): fine with either; prefers to ship it as soon as possible, Hegota is a good timeline.
  - Erigon (Milen): slight preference for Glamsterdam to avoid revisiting the topic, but happy with either.
  - ethrex (Iván): indicated preference for Hegota.
- Toni suggested deferring the final decision to Thursday's ACD call to let clients coordinate async and evaluate the change.
- Agreement: decision deferred to Thursday ACD call. Dan will add it to the ACD agenda.

sections.heading: EIP-8037 SELFDESTRUCT State-Gas Refill PR Closure
sections.summary: No objections to closing EIPs#12249; decision from ACDC last week stands.
sections.body:
- [EIPs#12249](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12249) (EIP-8037 SELFDESTRUCT state-gas refill) was declined at ACDC last week. PR is still open.
- No one on the call objected to closing it. Dan will ping Pablo (the author) to close.
- Jochem noted he has opened an ephemeral accounts channel on EF R&D to help affected users explore alternative patterns, particularly EIP-8360 (Create opcode), so that self-destruct usage is not incentivized.

sections.heading: Benchmarking Updates
sections.summary: Carlos will present Jochemnet vs State Actor benchmarking results for Geth at tomorrow's benchmarking call; State Actor likely becomes the reference going forward.
sections.body:
- CPerezz flagged that for Geth, the Jochem snapshot was loading accounts from the journal and treating them as warm, which skewed benchmark results.
  - EIP-8038 gas numbers are unlikely to change based on this finding.
  - State Actor will likely replace Jochemnet as the reference snapshot for future benchmarks (Hegota and beyond).
- Dan suggested bringing the devnet 8 attack scenario (Platåberget JUMPDEST spam) to the benchmarking call tomorrow to discuss expressing such attacks as EEST tests for benchmarker integration.
- PK will forward the question to Rafael.

sections.heading: EL Reorg Testing
sections.summary: Consensus to build reorg test suite in Hive; CPerezz will lead development, including PBT-derived and MPT reorg scenarios.
sections.body:
- CPerezz raised the lack of a general, cross-client reorg testing framework. Individual clients test reorgs internally, but there is no shared suite to prevent issues like the MPT-related bug in the latest mainnet Rev fork.
  - Context: [pm#2209 comment](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2209#issuecomment-5567858868)
- Client preferences:
  - Geth (Marius): slight preference for Hive to avoid creating another tool; Hive already has some sync/reorg tests.
  - Besu (Ben Adams): Hive would be good.
  - Nethermind (Karim): Hive makes sense.
- Dan suggested developing reorg tests within EEST format (with FCU directives added), which could then also support benchmark-specific reorg tests. CPerezz agreed and noted performance measurement for large reorg windows would be valuable.
- Toni shared [EIP-8252](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8252) as a reference for reorg window work.
- CPerezz confirmed: will start building in Hive, incorporating PBT reorg testing and MPT scenarios. No work required from client teams.

sections.heading: eth/72 txsize Ambiguity for Type-3 Transactions
sections.summary: Most clients already fixed the type-3 transaction size announcement issue; Stefan's devp2p PR to clarify the spec is open for async review.
sections.body:
- Carried over from ACDT #94. In eth/72, transaction size announcements for type-3 (blob) transactions were ambiguous because the actual data is in the sidecar, leading clients to expect different sizes and downscoring peers.
- Stefan created PRs against affected clients; most have merged fixes.
  - Besu fix merged: [besu-eth/besu#11203](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/pull/11203)
  - devp2p spec clarification PR: [devp2p#281](https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/pull/281)
  - EIP-8070 size_i follow-up: [EIPs#12275](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12275)
- No major discussion needed; feedback can be left async on the PR.

sections.heading: EIP-8037 State Gas in Debug Traces (RPC Standards)
sections.summary: State-gas trace field format headed to RPC Standards Call at 15:00 UTC today; Marius prefers a vector format for extensibility.
sections.body:
- [execution-apis#852](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/852) proposes how to surface state gas vs execution gas in debug traces, a Glamsterdam-specific change.
- Chase has made progress on RPC compatibility testing in Hive; updates are ready for review.
- Marius suggested making the trace field a `<stategas, execution>` vector to allow easy extension as more gas types are introduced in future forks.
- Stefan confirmed the PR is aligned with this approach. Discussion and hopefully finalization to happen at the RPC Standards Call ([pm#2213](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2213)) immediately after this call.
